    res=[]
    for f in range(3):
        # positions f, f+3, ...

## Report on `region.fasta` (sequence `>region_009`)

**Sequence:** 3,000 bp, single record. Overall G+C = 46.3%. No ambiguity codes, no repeats ≥25 bp, no inverted repeats ≥12 bp (no candidate hairpin/terminator), and no homopolymer tracts of note.

### 1. The sequence is not compositionally uniform
Sliding-window G+C reveals three blocks:

| Coordinates | G+C | Comment |
|---|---|---|
| 1–1200 | ~50% | typical of a bacterial-type genome |
| ~1200–2030 | **~34%** | markedly A+T-rich; atypical |
| ~2030–3000 | ~53% | high G+C |

The 800-bp A+T-rich block is the single most anomalous compositional feature. In an *E. coli*-like background (≈51% G+C) an 800-bp stretch at 34% G+C is not expected and is the kind of signature associated with recently acquired/foreign DNA.

### 2. A long, unambiguous membrane-protein gene on the + strand
**ORF1: 271–1158 (+ strand), 296 aa, stop codon at 1159–1161.**

- Codon usage is strongly protein-coding: GC1 0.51, GC2 0.39, **GC3 0.62** (the high-3rd-position/low-2nd-position pattern).
- The protein is very hydrophobic (mean Kyte–Doolittle 0.89) with **~7–8 predicted transmembrane helices**, approximately at residues 9–28, 38–58, 72–96, 102–123, 127–160, 178–199, 209–236 and 266–292.
- This is a small multi-spanning integral membrane protein — most consistent with a transporter/permease-type function. I could not assign a specific family (no homology search available), but the architecture is clear.
- No recognizable Shine–Dalgarno element was found in the 20 bp upstream of the ATG.

The same + strand reading frame is also largely stop-free across 262–1158, so ORF1 is the only substantial gene in the 5′ half.

### 3. Two shorter hydrophobic ORFs inside the A+T-rich block
Both on the + strand, tandemly arranged:

- **1220–1633 (+), 138 aa** (stop-free frame extends 1169–1633)
- **1650–2027 (+), 126 aa** (stop-free frame extends 1605–2027); a plausible RBS (`GGAG`) lies just upstream of its ATG

Both translations are hydrophobic and membrane-protein-like. They are long enough (138 and 126 codons of stop-free sequence in a 34% G+C context, where stops should be *more* frequent than average) that they are unlikely to be spurious, but their codon-usage signature is flat (GC3 ≈ 0.29–0.33), so this is the least confident part of the analysis.

### 4. A second extended ORF on the − strand, overlapping a + strand ORF at the 3′ end
- **2076–2676 (− strand), 200 aa** (ATG at forward coordinate 2675, stop ending at 2076). Codon signature is strongly coding-like (GC1 0.57, GC2 0.31, **GC3 0.70**).
- The − strand frame containing it is actually stop-free all the way to the region boundary (forward 2076–2999, 308 codons), i.e. **this gene may run off the end of the supplied region**.
- **2526–2963 (+ strand), 146 aa** (ATG at 2526), codon signature GC1 0.57, GC2 0.34, GC3 0.68 — also protein-like.

These two overlap over roughly **2526–2676 (~150 bp)**, which would be a conventional overlapping-gene arrangement.

More strikingly, over approximately **2403–2999 the + strand frame 3 and the − strand frame 2 are both essentially stop-free (~600 bp of double-coding)**. Over 900 bp at the extreme 3′ end (≈2100–3000), the two strands' favoured frames contain essentially no stop codons while both show protein-like third-position G+C. A random sequence would be expected to contain ~14 stops per reading frame over that length, so this degree of mutual stop-depletion is not explainable by chance.

### Caveats
- I had no database/homology search available, so none of the genes can be named; all functional statements are inferences from composition and hydropathy.
- Because the double-coding signal at the 3′ end (and the sharp 34% G+C block) is so far outside what a normal genomic sequence shows, an alternative explanation is that this record is a **chimeric or deliberately constructed sequence** (e.g. assembled from multiple sources, or engineered to encode overlapping reading frames). The A+T-rich block boundaries (~1200 and ~2030) coincide closely with changes in the set of long ORFs, which is consistent with a join between two different sequence sources.

### Summary of coordinates
| Feature | Coordinates | Strand | Size |
|---|---|---|---|
| A+T-rich anomalous block | ~1200–2030 | – | 830 bp, 34% G+C |
| ORF1, ~7–8 TM membrane protein | 271–1158 | + | 296 aa |
| ORF2, hydrophobic | 1220–1633 | + | 138 aa |
| ORF3, hydrophobic (GGAG RBS) | 1650–2027 | + | 126 aa |
| ORF4, soluble-type, runs to region edge | 2076–2676 | − | 200 aa (frame stop-free to 2999) |
| ORF5, protein-like | 2526–2963 | + | 146 aa |
| Dual-coding region (both strands stop-free) | ~2403–2999 | both | ~600 bp |

The clearest, most defensible finding is **ORF1 (271–1158), a strongly hydrophobic multi-transmembrane protein**; the most unusual findings are the **34% G+C block at ~1200–2030** and the **extensive opposite-strand overlapping coding at ~2403–2999**.
